title: PuzzleAtlas Style Pack
description: A standalone, pluggable file that sets the visual and tonal norms for a hunt's player-facing presentation (Preview and, eventually, the Player App). Referenced by a Hunt document as hunt.stylePack. Does not affect the Studio's own editor chrome — only the content players see.

schemaVersion.description: Style-pack schema version, independent of the hunt schema version.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in the style pack picker.

description.description: One or two sentences describing the intended feel and use case.

vibe.description: Narrative/tone guidance for authors (and future AI-assisted drafting). Informational only — not rendered as CSS.

toneNotes.description: A sentence or two of writing-voice guidance, e.g. 'Clipped, present-tense, slightly hard-boiled.'

headingFont.description: CSS font-family value (comma-separated stack) used for titles, node headings, ending names.

bodyFont.description: CSS font-family value used for scene/prompt body text.

monoFont.description: CSS font-family value for codes, answers-in-progress, evidence references. Falls back to bodyFont if omitted.

importUrl.description: Optional stylesheet URL (e.g. a Google Fonts link) the Studio may inject for live preview while authoring online. Not required for offline play — offline packaging of actual font files is a later, separate media-pipeline concern.

accent2.description: CSS colour. Secondary highlight, used sparingly.

families.description: Optional accent colours per node family, for any presentation surface that distinguishes them (e.g. open-leads list, evidence casebook).

shape.description: Controls how sharp/soft the player-facing UI feels.

imagery.description: Default treatment applied to any image content within a node once media support exists. Forward-looking — not yet consumed by Phase 1 text-only nodes.

filterCss.description: Explicit CSS filter() value implementing the treatment, e.g. 'grayscale(1) sepia(0.3) contrast(1.1)'.
